newsitem.title: UK: Broad EMU expectations gain this week - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Broad EMU expectations gain this week - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European economic and monetary union (EMU) edged higher in the past week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

Of the ten European countries monitored by JP Morgan, only Sweden registered a decline in its chances of joining the single currency at its start, according to JP Morgan's "EMU calculator," which is derived from the interest-rate swaps market.
Sweden's first wave EMU prospects dipped to 64 percent from 65 percent in the previous week.
The probability of France and Belgium joining Germany in monetary union on schedule in 1999 was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.

Italy's perceived chances of entering EMU were up to 74 percent from a 73 percent rating last week. The probability of Spain and Portugal joining were also up with Spain at 81 percent from 78 percent a week ago and Portugal up to 79 percent against 76.

Britain, viewed as the least likely country to join EMU at its start, saw its probability rise to 23 percent from 17 percent. Ireland, meantime, gained over ten percentage points to 61 percent against 50 percent a week ago.
JP Morgan said there was a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
